newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed sharply lower for the second successive day as strong U.S. economic data undermined global debt markets.
Dealers said the fall in the prices of state loans came in light trading with most activity in the so-called mark-bloc taking place in the more-liquid Bund futures contract.
"People just let it go to see where it went," one dealer said of the reluctance of buyers to take advantage of the market slump to pick up paper at lower levels.
He said the market remained weak, adding however that he saw Bunds finding support early next week.
The dive in debt markets in the afternoon occurred in two waves, prompted by non-farm payrolls figures and the National Association of Purchasing Managers index, both for July.
The data, stronger than forecast, were seen as increasing the chances of a tightening of U.S. monetary policy.
Another dealer said he saw some limited buying of Dutch bonds in the falling market.
"A lot of people were really puzzled by what went on," he said, adding that the September Bund contract could dip further next week toward support he sees at about 102.30.
The sell-off was most severe among shorter paper, sparking a further flattening of the guilder yield curve.
But the weakness in Dutch bonds was not as marked as in Bunds, a situation reflected in a widening of the Dutch yield discount to Germany in 10 year and longer paper.
A trader said that rather than look to buy, his clients were looking to sell Dutch bonds when the 10 year yield spread to Germany reached seven or eight basis points, the level where they ended.
